# Props only the structural answer lists

## Summary

- Verdict: almost all of the 48,940 props (16,002 chakra-only, 32,938 gate-large) are not a gap in the checker answer. 48,924 are inherited HTML/ARIA/DOM-event attributes that the checker answer keeps as a collapsed inheritance layer (`htmlElement` set) instead of listing them; the structural answer lists the same layer as a collapsed entry and also spells every attribute out as an own prop. Same inputs, same `extract` flags (default `--html-attributes full`), different representation.
- A real omission by the checker answer exists for 16 props in 8 component entries (5 of them in gate-large, 3 chakra-only repeated there): the checker lists zero or too few props where TypeScript has them. See "Real omissions".
- Checked with the real compiler API (TypeScript 6.0.3, script `ts-keys.cjs`): TypeScript's own type for every sampled component contains the attributes, so the structural list is right on names and the checker answer is right only if the consumer expands the layer.
- Residual risk in the representation: the layer carries only `htmlElement`, `typeName`, `omitted` names and `totalProps: 0`; no member list. A consumer that reads only `props` and `propSets` sees no `onClick`.

## How it was measured

- Inputs: `chakra-only.diff.json`, `gate-large.diff.json` (rows with `cls == only_struct`), the `.checker.json` and `.struct.json` files in this directory. Every one of the 48,940 rows has origin `own` in the structural answer.
- Whether a prop is "missing" was tested against the checker component's `inheritance[]` (layer `htmlElement`, `omitted`, `members`) and `notableInherited`, then against TypeScript.
- Components affected: 60 in chakra-only, 123 in gate-large.

## Group 1: HTML attributes, ARIA, DOM event handlers (48,924 props)

- Composition (both fixtures): handlers (`on*`) 29,382; aria-* 9,270; other HTML/global attributes 10,288 (className, style, slot, part, lang, nonce, role, tabIndex, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, suppressHydrationWarning, itemType, resource, ... and SVG attributes for ChakraIcon).
- Top 20 prop names, chakra-only (components affected, out of 60): children 58; then 57 each: aria-activedescendant, onDrag, onAuxClickCapture, aria-current, onWheelCapture, onFocus, onPasteCapture, aria-posinset, onLoadStart, onTimeUpdateCapture, onPointerCancel, aria-multiselectable, onTransitionEnd, className, onVolumeChangeCapture, onTouchEndCapture, onInput, onClickCapture, onDragEnterCapture.
- Top 20 prop names, gate-large (components affected, out of 123): 118 each: onScroll, aria-checked, onKeyPress, onContextMenu, aria-rowcount, aria-brailleroledescription, onTouchCancelCapture, onCompositionEnd, onDrop, aria-readonly, aria-rowindextext, onWaiting, onAuxClickCapture, onAnimationEnd, onLoad, onTouchEndCapture, onTransitionRunCapture, onTouchStart, aria-rowindex, onPlayCapture. The tail is global attributes (slot, part, lang, nonce, 118 each).
- The counts are flat (57 or 118) because every one of these is the full `@types/react` attribute set of an element, applied to every component that composes it. Per component: ChakraIcon 414 (SVG attributes), ChakraDatePickerInput 302, ChakraCloseButton and the other Chakra triggers 285, MuiTextareaAutosize 291.
- Layers in the checker answer for those components (chakra-only): `ComponentPropsWithoutRef` with htmlElement div (26), button (9), span (5), table (4), label (2), select (2), td (2). gate-large adds `React.HTMLAttributes` div (28), `React.ComponentPropsWithRef` a (13) and div (11).
- Verdict (a), not a gap: collapsed layer. In the checker JSON, ChakraCloseButton has `inheritance[1] = {typeName: ComponentPropsWithoutRef, htmlElement: "button", totalProps: 0, omitted: [847 names already listed as own]}` and lists 852 own props (style props), none of the HTML ones. In the structural JSON the same two layers exist unchanged, but the HTML attributes are also materialised as 431 own props. The attributes are present in meaning; the structural output states them twice.
- Structural duplication is the odd one: structural has an `htmlElement` layer and the same attributes as own props, with origin `own`, so a consumer merging layers would see duplicates.

## Group 2: sampled components checked against TypeScript

- Method: `ts-keys.cjs` loads the fixture tsconfig, takes the type of the first parameter of the component function (`ComponentProps<typeof X>`) and lists its property names. Run: `TSPATH=<typescript@6.0.3>/lib/typescript.js node ts-keys.cjs <fixture> <Component>...`. The repo's own `node_modules/typescript` is 7.x (native, no JS API), so a 6.0.3 copy from a worktree's pnpm store was used.
- ChakraCloseButton (chakra, button): TypeScript has 1,139 keys including onClick, aria-label, className, style, children, tabIndex, onDrag, title. Checker lists none of the attributes as props, only as the button layer. Not a gap.
- ChakraIcon (chakra, SVG): 1,262 keys including onClick, aria-label, className, style, onDrag; no `title` or `value` in the list. Structural lists 554 props, checker 846 plus layer. Not a gap.
- MuiTab (Mui, `DetailedHTMLProps` button): 301 keys; checker lists 25 own props and a layer. Not a gap.
- MuiTextareaAutosize (Mui, textarea): 294 keys; TypeScript has no `children` or `rows` for this component, and the checker layer `omitted` is exactly `["children","rows"]`. So the structural answer is wrong for those two (it lists `children` and `rows`-style props the component type omits; `children` is in the chakra top list at 58 for the same reason). Verdict (a) for the attributes, structural wrong on children/rows.
- ChakraDatePickerPropsProvider (chakra, context provider): TypeScript has 2 keys, children and value. Checker lists 0 props. Real omission, see below.
- MuiTableCell (Mui): TypeScript has 295 keys including className and style; checker lists 11 own props and no className/style. Real omission, see below.

## Option and representation check

- Same flags in both runs (`run-extract.sh`): `extract --json --quiet --no-cache --src <fixture>/src`, the second with `--no-checker`. No `--html-attributes`, no `--config`, so `htmlAttributes` is `full` in both and `collapseInheritedProps` has its default (collapse of loaded dependency files, threshold 30 props). No differing `skipHtmlProps`, `loadDependencies` or collapse option explains the difference.
- Collapsed layer in JSON: an entry in `inheritance[]` with `typeName`, `fileName`, `omitted` (names listed elsewhere), `htmlElement` and `totalProps`. For HTML layers `totalProps` is 0 and there is no `members`; for collapsed non-HTML layers (Chakra `SystemProperties`, 706 props) `members` carries the names. Both runs have identical `inheritance[]` for the sampled components; only the checker leaves the attribute props out of `props`.
- Consequence: a prop inside a collapsed HTML layer is not missing, but it is only discoverable via `htmlElement` plus @types/react, not from the JSON alone.

## Real omissions (b): checker answer drops props TypeScript has

- 16 props, 8 component entries across both fixtures (the 3 Chakra provider components appear in both fixtures).
- ChakraDatePickerPropsProvider, ChakraIconPropsProvider, ChakraSkeletonPropsProvider (chakra-only and gate-large) and MuiSelectFocusSourceProvider (gate-large): `ComponentProps<typeof X>` where X is a React context `Provider`. TypeScript gives `ProviderProps<T>` = `{ value: T; children?: ReactNode }`. The checker answer lists no props, only `composes: ["ProviderProps"]`. Structural lists `value` (required) and `children`. Why: the checker lane does not expand `ProviderProps` (a generic interface applied to an unresolved context value type) and records no layer for it.
- MuiTableCell (gate-large): `ComponentProps<typeof TableCell>` is an intersection of `Th`/`Td` HTML attributes. The checker lists 11 own props and `composes: ["ThHTMLAttributes","TdHTMLAttributes"]` with no inheritance layer, so `className` and `style` are absent while TypeScript has them (and the other 293 attributes). Structural lists className and style as own props. Why: a union of two element attribute types (th/td) gets no single `htmlElement`, so no layer is emitted either.
- Scale: 16 of 48,940 (0.03%). They are worth a fix because a context provider answer with zero props is plainly wrong.

## Not a gap, structural wrong

- MuiTextareaAutosize `children` and `rows`: TypeScript's type omits them (component declares `Omit<TextareaHTMLAttributes, 'children' | 'rows'>`); the checker's `omitted` agrees, structural lists them. Counted inside the 48,924.

## Not done

- Oracle, corpus runs and extract re-runs were not run. The 5 sampled components plus the providers were checked with TypeScript; the other 178 components were judged by the same layer structure (htmlElement present in 175 of 183).

- `less precise`, `wrong`, `missing`: Caliper's type is looser, describes something else, or the prop is not listed.
- `opaque with marker`: less precise, and Caliper said so (`degradedBy` on the prop). A marked type is honest; an unmarked `less precise` is a silent loss. A `wrong` type stays `wrong` with a marker.
- `checker any/error`: the golden itself has no type. That is a broken fixture, not a result.

A row is green or a documented gap. A gap lists the verdicts it may have, none of them green, and a `gap` reason. Trail 394 side finding: with the checker on, caliper omitted props TypeScript gives a component that has no inheritance layer.
